facts.text: The clone is a Python 2.7 module: line 341 is a print statement, so the Python 3 ast parser cannot read the file
The module constructs SMBus(1) at import time and talks to the AS7265x at I2C address 0x49
init() writes register 0x04 with 1 and sleeps 4 seconds after the factory reset
boardPresent() reads register 0x00 and returns True or False
hwVersion() reads registers 0x00 and 0x01 and returns a tuple of the device type and hardware version
temperatures() selects AS72651, AS72652 and AS72653 and reads register 0x06 from each into a list of three values
setBlueLED(state) selects AS72651 and writes bit 0 of register 0x07
shutterLED(device,state) selects one of AS72651, AS72652 or AS72653 and writes bit 3 of register 0x07
setLEDDriveCurrent accepts 0, 1, 2 or 3 and writes bits 4-5 of register 0x07 on all three devices; the docstring maps them to 12.5, 25, 50 and 100 mA
setIntegrationTime checks range(0,255), so it accepts 0 through 254, and writes register 0x05 on all three devices; the docstring says 0 to 255
setGain accepts 0, 1, 2 or 3 and writes bits 4-5 of register 0x04 on all three devices; the docstring maps them to 1x, 3.7x, 16x and 64x
readRAW() reads six 16-bit register pairs from each of the three devices, giving 18 raw values, and reorders them into ascending frequency order
readCAL() reads six IEEE754 quadruples from each of the three devices, giving 18 calibrated values, and reorders them into ascending frequency order
reorderData maps the 18 values from the device read order to the monotonic frequency order
The README calls the project a Python module to drive the SparkFun Triad Spectroscopy Sensor
The board consists of three devices with six sensors each and passbands from UV to IR; the three on-board LEDs peak at about 400, 475 and 875 nm
The README targets Python 2.7 on a Raspberry Pi 3B
The README lists setIntegrationTime legal input values 0 to 255, setGain 0 to 3 and setLEDDriveCurrent 0 to 3
The README says readRAW and readCAL return 18 values sorted into ascending frequency order
